events.title: Columbus Secures Royal Backing for His Voyage
events.description: In the town of Santa Fe, near Granada, Christopher Columbus and the Spanish Crown signed the Capitulations of Santa Fe. The agreement set out the titles, authority and share of profits Columbus would receive if his planned expedition across the Atlantic succeeded.
events.significance: The agreement made Columbus's first voyage possible. It launched a period of European contact with the Americas that reshaped the world.

events.title: The Bay of Pigs Invasion Begins
events.description: A force of Cuban exiles, trained and backed by the United States, landed at the Bay of Pigs on Cuba's southern coast. They hoped to spark an uprising against Fidel Castro. They met strong resistance from Cuban forces almost at once.
events.significance: The invasion failed. It embarrassed the young Kennedy administration, strengthened Castro's position and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union. That set the stage for the Cuban Missile Crisis the next year.

events.title: Jerrie Mock Completes a Solo Flight Around the World
events.description: Geraldine 'Jerrie' Mock landed back in Columbus, Ohio, having left on March 19. She flew a single-engine Cessna and became the first woman to fly solo around the globe.
events.significance: Mock's flight broke a major barrier in aviation. It showed that women could take on the longest and most demanding flights.

events.title: Apollo 13 Splashes Down Safely
events.description: The crippled Apollo 13 spacecraft parachuted into the Pacific Ocean, less than a mile from the recovery ship. An onboard explosion had forced the crew to abandon their Moon landing and use the lunar module as a lifeboat for the trip home.
events.significance: The safe return of all three astronauts is remembered as one of the great rescues in the history of spaceflight. It is often called a 'successful failure' for the ingenuity of the crew and Mission Control.
